subject.title: [Bug]: GitHub Copilot anthropic-messages transport silently hangs ~365s in isolated cron sessions (2026.5.27)

question: Should aborted no-output Copilot cron runs be eligible for automatic fallback by default, or should OpenClaw only surface them as hard runtime errors unless an explicit fallback model is configured?
rationale: Current source intentionally excludes `meta.aborted` terminal results from fallback classification, while the issue asks for fallback behavior and reliable failure surfacing across a provider-specific transport path.

options.title: Keep Open For Fallback Policy
options.body: Keep #87692 open until maintainers choose the default fallback/error policy and land live Copilot proof for that policy.

options.title: Split To Narrow Issues
options.body: Use #97290 for default fallback candidates and keep this issue only for transport hang proof and diagnostics.

options.title: Error-Only Recovery
options.body: Declare aborted no-output cron runs a hard provider/runtime error and document that fallback requires explicit configured candidates.

recommendation.title: Keep Open For Fallback Policy
recommendation.body: Keep #87692 open until maintainers choose the default fallback/error policy and land live Copilot proof for that policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The current history points most strongly to Peter Steinberger across the Copilot stream wrapper, embedded agent runner, and cron abort-status proof paths.
